question_text: A 24-year-old woman presents with a 3-month history of worsening insomnia and anxiety. She says that she has an important college exam in the next few weeks for which she has to put in many hours of work each day. Despite the urgency of her circumstances, she states that she is unable to focus and concentrate, is anxious, irritable and has lost interest in almost all activities. She also says that she has trouble falling asleep and wakes up several times during the night. She claims that this state of affairs has severely hampered her productivity and is a major problem for her, and she feels tired and fatigued all day. She denies hearing voices, abnormal thoughts, or any other psychotic symptoms. The patient asks if there is some form of therapy that can help her sleep better so that she can function more effectively during the day. She claims that the other symptoms of not enjoying anything, irritability, and anxiety are things that she can learn to handle. Which of the following approaches is most likely to address the patients concerns most effectively?

                    ### Question
                    A 24-year-old woman presents with a 3-month history of worsening insomnia and anxiety. She says that she has an important college exam in the next few weeks for which she has to put in many hours of work each day. Despite the urgency of her circumstances, she states that she is unable to focus and concentrate, is anxious, irritable and has lost interest in almost all activities. She also says that she has trouble falling asleep and wakes up several times during the night. She claims that this state of affairs has severely hampered her productivity and is a major problem for her, and she feels tired and fatigued all day. She denies hearing voices, abnormal thoughts, or any other psychotic symptoms. The patient asks if there is some form of therapy that can help her sleep better so that she can function more effectively during the day. She claims that the other symptoms of not enjoying anything, irritability, and anxiety are things that she can learn to handle. Which of the following approaches is most likely to address the patients concerns most effectively?

                    ### Options
                    opa. Psychotherapy only
opb. Initiation of risperidone
opc. Trial of bupropion
opd. Dose titration of mirtazapine
ope. Phototherapy

### Enhanced Information (For Contextual Support):
The patient presents with insomnia, anxiety, irritability, and loss of interest, which are indicative of a potential mood disorder, likely depression. Mirtazapine is an antidepressant that is effective in treating both sleep disturbances and anxiety symptoms, making it a suitable option for this patient. Psychotherapy may provide coping strategies but is less likely to directly address her sleep issues. Bupropion is primarily used for depression and smoking cessation but is not effective for insomnia. Risperidone, an antipsychotic, is not indicated for her symptoms as she denies psychotic features. Phototherapy is typically used for seasonal affective disorder and does not align with her current symptoms. Therefore, the most effective approach to address her concerns is the dose titration of mirtazapine, which can improve her sleep quality and overall functioning.
